articles.title: “Three years ago…”: Kirk Cousins opens up about difficult years after emotional Vikings return ends with Packers victory
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins struggled to hold back his tears after leading the Minnesota Vikings to a 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, November 15.
articles.body: Kirk Cousins struggled to hold back his tears after leading the Minnesota Vikings to a 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, November 15. The victory was especially personal for the 38-year-old quarterback, who returned to Lambeau Field just three years after suffering a serious Achilles injury there. Speaking to ESPN after the game, Cousins opened up about a difficult period in his career and admitted how much the return meant to him.Kirk Cousins gets emotional after Vikings beat Packers in his first game backCousins had plenty of reasons to feel emotional after Sunday’s game. In his postgame interview with ESPN reporter Lindsey Thiry, he spoke about the memories of his last appearance at Lambeau Field, where he tore his Achilles tendon on October 29, 2023. That injury ended his season and turned out to be his final game for Minnesota during his first spell with the team.“It was emotional coming to the stadium,” Cousins told Thiry. “Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It’s been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today, and grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible.”He also made it clear that he believes there is more ahead for him, adding, “There’s more to this story being written.”The quarterback backed up his words with a strong performance. He completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns and one interception as Minnesota secured a comfortable win on the road. The result also improved the Vikings’ record to 7-2.For Cousins, however, the numbers were only one part of the story. Returning to the same stadium where his previous Vikings journey ended with a serious injury gave the win a personal meaning that went beyond the result.Kirk Cousins returns to Minnesota after difficult stints with Falcons and RaidersCousins originally joined the Vikings in 2018 and spent five seasons with the team before leaving for the Atlanta Falcons in 2024. His time in Atlanta brought its own challenges. The Falcons selected quarterback Michael Penix Jr. with the eighth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, shortly after signing Cousins. The veteran later said he felt “misled” by the team’s decision.He moved to the Las Vegas Raiders earlier in 2026, where he served as their starting quarterback while rookie Fernando Mendoza developed. However, his stay in Las Vegas did not last long. On November 10, the Raiders traded him back to Minnesota in exchange for a 2027 third-round draft pick, according to ESPN.The move came after Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was injured and Carson Wentz struggled while filling in. Cousins was suddenly given another chance with the team where he had spent some of the most important years of his career.Interestingly, the decision also involved his family. Cousins revealed that he and his wife, Julie Hampton Cousins, allowed their two sons, Cooper and Turner, to have a say in the move. Julie was concerned about taking the children away from their school, baseball activities and friends, but their response made the choice easier.“Let’s go,” the boys told their mother after she explained that their father had been traded to Minnesota.Cousins also spoke about his relationship with Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell, explaining that the coach understands both his strengths and weaknesses. That familiarity, he suggested, made returning to Minnesota a more comfortable decision.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Kylie Kelce is finally setting the record straight after months of backlash over her comments about husband Jason Kelce and their childcare arrangements. What started as a seemingly casual conversation about having a nanny turned into an internet debate about whether the former Philadelphia Eagles star was doing his fair share of parenting.And Kylie wasn't exactly happy about how people interpreted her words.Kylie Kelce says her comments about Jason were taken out of contextDuring her appearance on Cameron Oaks Rogers' podcast, Conversations With Cam, Cameron brought up the controversy while discussing their respective nannies. Cameron praised her own nanny, calling her a hero, before asking Kylie about the viral comments suggesting she wouldn't let Jason watch their children alone.Kylie didn't hold back when revisiting the situation, admitting that the reaction had made her angry for months."Oh yeah. It got so aggressively taken out of context that I was pissed about it for months," Kylie explained.She added that there eventually comes a point when continuing to defend yourself only brings more attention to the controversy. The mother of four also addressed the biggest misconception surrounding her original comments."People were like, 'You won't let Jason watch your kids.' And I'm like, 'What do you mean, let him watch the kids? They're his kids,'" she said.Kylie explained that the situation had much more to do with Jason's unpredictable professional schedule than his ability or willingness to look after their children.At the time, Jason was juggling football-season commitments with ESPN and several other responsibilities. His schedule could change without much warning, making it difficult for the couple to plan their childcare arrangements around his availability.According to Kylie, Jason could tell her he had nothing planned, only for someone to call him unexpectedly and keep him occupied for another 45 minutes to an hour.Why Kylie continued hiring a nanny even when Jason was homeKylie also clarified why she preferred arranging childcare whenever she knew she would be leaving the house. She explained that the decision was simply about making sure someone was available to look after their children when both parents had demanding schedules.However, the internet interpreted that arrangement as Kylie refusing to leave Jason alone with their daughters. She insisted that wasn't what she meant in the original conversation."If you go back and watch the clip, you can tell there's a sarcastic manner to the way I'm talking about it," Kylie explained.She pointed out that she had spoken about how busy both of them were at the time and how that led them to make sure childcare was available whenever she knew she wouldn't be home.But the headlines that followed told a completely different story.Kylie recalled how some reports suggested Jason never watched his children or that she hired a nanny even when he was available at home."And no," she added, pushing back against those interpretations.Kylie and Jason Kelce's family life under the spotlightThe couple, who married in 2018, share four daughters: Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finn. Since Jason's retirement from the NFL in 2024, the former Eagles center has remained busy with several football-related projects, including his work with ESPN's Monday Night Countdown.Meanwhile, Kylie has built her own career through her podcast, public appearances and charitable work. Their family life has also attracted plenty of attention thanks to Jason's growing media profile and Kylie's increasingly popular podcast.But this latest clarification makes one thing clear: Kylie wasn't suggesting that Jason couldn't handle parenting responsibilities. She was explaining how the couple managed childcare during an especially hectic period of their lives.And after months of people questioning their parenting arrangement, Kylie seems ready to put the controversy behind her.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Justin Herbert's world runs on football, Madison Beer's on music, but their relationship found common ground away from fame
articles.summary: Justin Herbert and Madison Beer are engaged.
articles.body: Justin Herbert and Madison Beer are engaged. The Chargers quarterback and the pop singer announced it on July 28 in a joint Instagram post with photos from the proposal. Beer’s caption was short: “Meet my fiancé.” The news came about eleven months after paparazzi first photographed them together on the set of a music video in August 2025. Since then, the couple has turned up at NFL sidelines, Lakers games and the World Series, and Herbert’s public messages about her have grown warmer with each passing month. The path from first photo to proposal took less than a year.Justin Herbert and Madison Beer found common ground in each other’s worldThe first photos surfaced on Aug. 17, 2025. Paparazzi caught Herbert and Beer close together on the set of an upcoming music video, which put the quarterback in her workplace instead of his. Neither had confirmed anything. US Weekly ran exclusive photos, and the dating talk spread fast.The secrecy did not last. On Oct. 5, Beer was photographed kissing Herbert on the sideline before the Chargers faced the Washington Commanders. A sideline before kickoff is about as public as it gets, and she looked at ease there.The next few days were busy. On Oct. 24, the pair sat courtside at Crypto.com Arena as the Lakers beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 128-110. They reportedly went to a Chargers Halloween party the following night. Then came Dodger Stadium on Oct. 27, for game three of the World Series between the Toronto Blue Jays and the Los Angeles Dodgers. Almost every outing centered on sports, which suggests Beer was meeting Herbert’s world on its own calendar.Beer kept showing up on Chargers game days. On Nov. 30, she watched the team beat the Las Vegas Raiders 31-14 with her mother, who was celebrating a birthday. Bringing family to a game says plenty about how settled a relationship feels.Birthday posts led to the engagementBy 2026, Herbert was not hiding much. On March 5, Beer’s 27th birthday, he posted photos of the two on Instagram Stories. He wrote, “Happy birthday to my favorite person of all time ... you’ve changed my life forever,” and added, “I am the luckiest guy alive.”April brought a shorter one. Herbert shared a photo with Beer under a two-word caption: “My world.”The posts are plain, and that is the point. Herbert’s public words mostly go to football. Here he was writing about a person, not a play.Look at the places again: a music video set, a sideline, courtside seats, a baseball stadium, a team party. Her world is music and his is football, and they kept turning up in each other’s. A team party and her mother at his game suggest she was brought into the real circle, not just the photo ops.The engagement came on July 28. Herbert and Beer posted together on Instagram, sharing photos from the proposal. Herbert’s teammates, according to SI’s reporting, already knew she was the “one,” which fits that picture.Eleven months separated the first photos from the engagement post. What the public record shows is steady progress: a couple seen together more often, then a quarterback putting his feelings into plain words for anyone to read. The proposal reads like the next step rather than a surprise.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer again declines to support DC Christian Parker after struggles, brutal loss to 49ers
articles.summary: Brian Schottenheimer said they are taking a "deep dive" at everything amid their defensive woes.
articles.body:
Brian Schottenheimer, at least publicly, isn't backing his defensive coordinator.

The Cowboys head coach didn't directly support defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Monday, one day after a brutal showing from the Dallas defense in its 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Instead, he said everything is still under review.

"We're still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer said, via The Dallas Morning News . "At the end of the day, there's a lot of things that we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me."

The 49ers racked up 584 yards of offense and averaged 9.4 yards per play in the win on Sunday. They ran for 214 yards, too, and put up 29 points and 340 yards in the second half alone. It was simply an offensive clinic that the Cowboys couldn't stop time and time again.

The 584 yards that Dallas allowed was the most they've allowed in a home game in franchise history.

Schottenheimer said after the game that he thought the defense was "unacceptable," and he called the tackling "atrocious."

"At the end of the day, we tackled like s**t in the second half," he said.

Dallas' defensive issues are nothing new. They've been a problem all season, and it's led to louder and louder calls to make a change at defensive coordinator. Parker is in his first season in the role, which also marks his first coordinator job in the NFL.

Though he declined to support Parker again on Monday, Schottenheimer did not say he was going to make a change.

"I'm not saying that," he said. "I'm saying we're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today."

Perhaps more importantly, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones did back Parker on Sunday afternoon.

"Again, it's what it is," Jones said postgame. "He's a young coach in his first year of coordinating and calling the plays. So you have to say that you would hope you could win games like the last that we've lost. "I'll weigh his early times. I've been with teams that had some pretty good coordinators on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls."

"Again, it's what it is," Jones said postgame. "He's a young coach in his first year of coordinating and calling the plays. So you have to say that you would hope you could win games like the last that we've lost.

"I'll weigh his early times. I've been with teams that had some pretty good coordinators on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls."

But instead of following Jones' lead, Schottenheimer said simply that they are "taking a deep dive" and "looking at everything."

The Cowboys are still in the playoff hunt despite their 4-6 record, thanks to a rough NFC East. They are only two games behind the New York Giants. They'll take on the Tennessee Titans next weekend. But the Cowboys haven't won a Super Bowl since the 1995 season, and this team doesn't appear capable of ending that streak.

The frustration that fans feel, vice president Stephen Jones said, is being felt internally, too.

"I certainly understand their frustration because there's no doubt that we're frustrated," the younger Jones said on 105.3 The Fan . "We feel like the way we're playing ball right now is unacceptable. Our fans certainly deserve better."

Whether the outcry and issues on defense result in a change at defensive coordinator before the end of the season, however, is still anybody's guess.

articles.body: Brian Schottenheimer’s job security has become the main talking point in Dallas, and the Cowboys have seven games left to settle it. Jerry Jones still sounds willing to give his head coach more time. Stephen Jones struck a more frustrated tone on 105.3 The Fan on Monday. The defense is the sore spot. It ranks as the league’s worst, and SI’s Gilberto Manzano believes one name could repair it: Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. His case is simple enough to state in one line. Dallas has tried other fixes and none has stuck.Brian Flores could fix the Cowboys defenseNot all of Schottenheimer’s defensive trouble is his fault, and Manzano admits it. His verdict is still blunt.“It’s become clear that Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer can’t fix this defense. Sure, it’s fair to say Schottenheimer got a raw deal when owner and GM Jerry Jones traded star edge rusher Micah Parsons two weeks before his first season last year. But Jones isn’t going anywhere to pay for his mistake, and he’s tried to upgrade this defense, trading for Quinnen Williams and Joey Porter Jr. It also didn’t work when the team fired defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus and hired Christian Parker to replace him,” Manzano wrote.That is the part Jones may like least. He has already tried the roster route and the coordinator route, and the numbers have not moved. Manzano then goes after the budget.“It’s time the Cowboys move on from Schottenheimer, especially if this team has no interest in rebuilding. The richest owner in sports needs to stop being cheap when it comes to paying top coaches and hire Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores to be the new head coach. He might be the only person who can drastically improve the league’s worst defense. The Cowboys aren’t going anywhere with a one-sided team, something that has been noticeable for a few years now.”Flores brings a clear picture of what a defense should look like. He is widely considered one of the most creative defensive minds in the game. He disguises coverages, so quarterbacks guess instead of read. He also gets pressure without needing an elite pass-rusher, which helps a roster that no longer has Micah Parsons. Mostly, he would give Dallas an identity.What Dallas would need to make it workA defensive head coach needs a partner on offense. That should not be hard to find. Dallas has Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and an elite offensive line, which would appeal to a proven play-caller.Jones has focused on offensive coaches so far. Flores would flip that thinking. Let a creative coordinator work with Prescott, and let Flores fix the side that has dragged the team down. Prescott is in his prime, and that window will not wait.Seven games remain, and Schottenheimer still has them. What his defense does in that stretch will decide whether Jones has to make this call.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Playoff Bracket Scenarios 2026-27 Week 11 After Herbert, Chargers Beat Brissett, Ravens
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens' playoff hopes took an even bigger hit on Monday night with a loss to the Los Angeles Chargers.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens' playoff hopes took an even bigger hit on Monday night with a loss to the Los Angeles Chargers.

The Chargers' first win of the 2026 NFL season dropped the Ravens to 4-6 and two games back of the final wild-card position in the AFC.

Jacoby Brissett and Co. now face an incredibly tough climb up to the No. 7 seed over the next two months because so many teams in the AFC are playing good football at the moment.

A lot of marquee matchups over the next two weeks will shake up the playoff standings, but for now, the Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers sit atop their respective conferences.

Baltimore is now two games back of the Cleveland Browns in the final wild-card spot after Monday's loss.

The Ravens already have a head-to-head loss to the Browns. That defeat started a five-game losing streak that they will carry into their Week 11 clash with the Carolina Panthers.

The good news, if there is any right now, is that the Ravens close the season with four straight AFC North clashes. They have the potential to make a miraculous run at a playoff spot if all goes well during that stretch.

However, Baltimore has to get to that spot in a decent position first. It visits Carolina and Houston before its Week 13 bye. Those aren't exactly two easy games.

The AFC North-leading Cincinnati Bengals will be under the spotlight next Monday on the road against the Washington Commanders.

While Cincinnati is the talk of the NFL right now, there's buzz already building toward Thanksgiving Day, when the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs face off.

That's the first of a few big games in a row for the Chiefs, who after Buffalo, take on the Los Angeles Rams and the Bengals on the road.

The NFC North and West are the only two divisions that should get multiple teams into the postseason bracket.

Two teams from those divisions, Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers, face off in the biggest NFC game of Week 11 on Sunday night.

The Vikings have found new life on offense with Kirk Cousins back in the fold. They went into Green Bay and dominated the Packers in Week 10 in Cousins' first game back in a Vikings uniform.

That's the first of a few massive NFC games to close out November that will dictate where the playoff standings are going into December.

The Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams meet on Thanksgiving Eve in a huge wild-card matchup and then the Chicago Bears visit the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day.

The 49ers are at home to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 12, a Sunday slate that also features the NFC South clash between the Carolina Panthers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night.

Carolina enters Week 11 with a one-game edge over Tampa Bay and the New Orleans Saints and a 1.5-game advantage over the Atlanta Falcons.

The New York Giants are safe, for now, atop the NFC East, but they have a tough next month ahead, starting with a visit from the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.

articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft order: Titans take over No. 1 spot after Chargers grab first win of season in Week 10
articles.summary: The Chargers have now joined the Jets and Titans at just 1-8 on the season.
articles.body:
It's never too early to start looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft, right?

Week 10 of the current NFL season wrapped up on Monday night, and the order for the draft in a few months is already starting to take shape.

And, at least for now, the Tennessee Titans have taken over control of the No. 1 pick. That's all thanks to the Los Angeles Chargers, who finally picked up their first win of the season on Monday night in Baltimore.

The Chargers, who entered Week 10 as the last winless team in the league, beat the Ravens 23-20 at M&T Bank Stadium . That marked the fifth straight loss for the Ravens, who now sit at 4-6 on the season.

The Chargers have now joined both the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins with 1-8 records. The Titans fell to the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 40-23 blowout on Sunday afternoon, which marked their third straight loss and moved them to 0-5 at Nissan Stadium this season. The Dolphins barely lost to the Indianapolis Colts 24-22 on Sunday. The win snapped the Colts' five-game losing skid, yet the victory moved them to only 3-7 on the year. The Dolphins have lost three straight heading into a road game against the Buffalo Bills next week.

Though all three teams share the same record, the Titans jumped the Chargers into the top spot through the tiebreaker. The Chargers sit at No. 2, and the Dolphins are at No. 3. The New York Jets and Philadelphia Eagles round out the top five.

Even though things are undoubtedly bad, the Chargers have finally gotten their first win. That felt inevitable, especially since the NFL hasn't seen a team go a full season without winning a game since the 2017 Cleveland Browns.

With several weeks to go in the regular season, any of those three teams can still absolutely claim the No. 1 overall pick down the stretch. The Jets and Eagles, both with just two wins this season, aren't out of the question yet, either.

For now, though, the Titans are in control of that top spot.

1. Tennessee Titans (1-8) 2. Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) 3. Miami Dolphins (1-8) 4. New York Jets (2-8) 5. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) 6. New York Jets (via 3-7 Indianapolis Colts) 7. Arizona Cardinals (3-7) 8. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 9. Houston Texans (3-6) 10. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) 11. New Orleans Saints (3-6) 12. Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 13. New York Jets (via 4-6 Dallas Cowboys) 14. Baltimore Ravens (4-6) 15. Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) 16. New England Patriots (5-5) 17. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 18. articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 10 Results as Chargers' 1st Win Shakes Up No. 1 Pick Race
articles.summary: It finally happened—the Los Angeles Chargers got a win.
articles.body:
It finally happened—the Los Angeles Chargers got a win.

John Harbaugh's beleaguered Chargers defeated the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night, 23-20, a result that—at least temporarily—had major implications for April's draft.

Here's how L.A.'s win impacted the current 2027 NFL draft order:

There's plenty of season left, of course. But should the Titans remain at No. 1, they'll have a very interesting choice to make.

With Cam Ward already on the roster, it's hard to imagine quarterback being a consideration unless they decide after just two seasons that he's not the guy. More than likely, however, they would decide between three options—Ohio State wideout Jeremiah Smith, Texas edge-rusher Colin Simmons or trading back to accumulate more draft assets.

Smith is the best receiver in college football, registering 80 catches for 1,317 yards and 15 touchdowns. He might be the safest bet at receiver in years and looks like a plug-and-play difference-maker at the next level.

But Simmons may be just as dynamic on the defensive side of the ball. The Texas standout has 10.5 sacks, 16 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery this season. It's hard to imagine him being on the board for long.

One interesting factor to consider, however, is that teams in the top 10 like the Miami Dolphins, New York Jets, Arizona Cardinals and maybe even the Atlanta Falcons could be in the market for a quarterback. That could create a nice bidding war for the Titans (or perhaps even for the Chargers at No. 2).

The draft order is sure to change as the season progresses, but we have a pretty good idea of which teams are likely to be hovering around the top five come April.

articles.title: Kaelon Black and the Best Week 11 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: Bye-mageddon is upon us.
articles.body:
With a 2026 NFL season-high six teams out on break in Week 11, fantasy football managers will be rushing to the waiver wire in hopes of finding players who can help them through this tough stretch.

Whether you need a quarterback to replace your regular starter, a running back with decent rest-of-season value or a high-upside wideout to roll the dice on, there are several quality candidates who fit the bill still up for grabs in most leagues.

While there's an unfortunate lack of potential league-winners sitting in free agency, there is enough serviceable talent to help teams engaged in heated races for coveted playoff spots notch a win. With that in mind, here's a look at the best waiver-wire targets for Week 11.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings are courtesy of FantasyPros ' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Cam Ward, Tennessee Titans (9 Percent Rostered)

Cam Ward's sophomore season hasn't gone as well as fans in the Music City may have hoped, but the young signal-caller has been displaying glimpses of improvement over the last few weeks.

Ward has sandwiched a pair of top-12 finishes between Tennessee's Week 10 bye, including a career-best 26.3-point outing against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. While he couldn't reach those same lofty heights on Sunday, he did ring up an impressive 20.1 points against a stingy Jacksonville Jaguars defense.

Expect Ward to clear the 20-point mark again in Week 11 when the Titans take on the Dallas Cowboys. Dallas' sieve-like defense has been allowing opposing quarterbacks to utterly feast, including this past weekend, when Brock Purdy shredded the unit for nearly 400 yards through the air and finished with 31.7 points.

Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers (46 Percent Rostered)

Aaron Rodgers has cooled off significantly since posting four consecutive top-13 finishes from Weeks 3-6, but he has an ideal opportunity to get back on track in Week 11.

The Steelers will be looking to bounce back from a disappointing Sunday Night Football defeat when they make a trip across Pennsylvania to face the Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles are allowing 25 fantasy points per game to opposing passers in 2026, the fifth-highest mark in football.

With Philly well out of contention and the Steelers still fighting for their playoff lives, Rodgers should dial things in and post borderline QB1 numbers in what could be a high-scoring contest. The 42-year-old is far from a long-term solution for QB-needy managers, but he'll get the job done for Week 11.

Jacoby Brissett is poised to make his second start since he was traded to the Ravens at the deadline, when his new team visits the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. While it remains to be seen how quickly the journeyman picks up a new offense, he's Baltimore's best hope of turning this disappointing campaign around and should get ample opportunity to move the ball downfield.

Brissett had some strong games for the Arizona Cardinals earlier in the year, including a 25.6-point outing against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 3 and a 25.3-point showing versus the Detroit Lions two weeks later. He likely won't come close to averaging the 38.1 pass attempts per game he had for the Cards, but he should be more efficient with a better ground attack supporting him in Charm City.

While Brissett's floor is concerningly low heading, he has more upside than most budget waiver-wire quarterbacks you could put a claim in on this week and is worth a gamble.

Kaelon Black, San Francisco 49ers (39 Percent Rostered)

Kaelon Black can no longer be written off as nothing more than Christian McCaffrey's handcuff. While that status does give him enough fantasy value to warrant rostering in many leagues, he's now offering plenty of standalone value as a key member of San Francisco's backfield timeshare.

Black has earned 11-plus carries in each of the last three games and just had the best fantasy performance of his young career, turning 11 totes into 53 yards and a score against the Dallas Cowboys. He was also slightly more involved in the passing game than usual, catching both of his targets for 13 additional yards.

While Black's 14.6-point performance doesn't jump off the page, it was a good first-ever top-20 finish and gives him flex appeal going forward. The Niners clearly want to keep McCaffrey fresh for their inevitable playoff run by working his backup in often, evidenced by the 40-plus percent offensive snap share Black has logged in two of the last three games.

Whether you want to protect your McCaffrey investment, pad out your depth with a decent fill-in RB with elite upside or simply need to plug a hole in the starting lineup for Week 11, Black checks every box and should be your top priority target on waivers.

Seth McGowan, Indianapolis Colts (18 Percent Rostered)

Seth McGowan has surprisingly remained fantasy relevant despite the Colts' decision not to trade away superstar running back Jonathan Taylor at the deadline.

While Taylor's continued presence significantly downgrades McGowan's rest-of-season outlook, the rookie has shown he can still make an impact from his backup role. Despite playing just 17 offensive snaps in Week 10, McGowan had an extremely efficient 77 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries. It marked the second straight week the 25-year-old found pay dirt and posted a top-16 fantasy finish.

Most managers who were hanging onto McGowan as a lottery ticket opted to drop him after Indy elected not to move Taylor earlier in the week. That could be a huge mistake if McGowan continues to thrive as the team's RB2 or takes over as the starter due to injury.

McGowan is currently available in more than 80 percent of fantasy leagues, a number that should shrink significantly after his latest performance. Don't hesitate to fire him up if you need a high-upside RB3 or flex option this week.

Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jacksonville Jaguars (37 Percent Rostered)

Chris Rodriguez is far from the most exciting fantasy player to put in your starting lineup, but desperate managers who need someone to use during bye-mageddon could do far worse than the Jags' No. 2 rusher.

While Rodriguez doesn't see much work in the passing game and is the junior partner behind Bhayshul Tuten in Jacksonville's backfield platoon, he's seeing enough carries most weeks to warrant flex consideration. He posted RB21 and RB19 finishes in consecutive weeks leading up to Week 10 before plummeting outside the top-60 with an ugly 0.5-point showing against the Tennessee Titans.

Rodriguez may be coming off a terrible game, but a beatable New York Giants rush defense and a decent amount of projected volume give him an edge over most backs still available in deeper leagues.

Ryan Flournoy, Dallas Cowboys (49 Percent Rostered)

Ryan Flournoy has come into his own during his third NFL season. While there's not much left over after accounting for the looks both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens see each week, Flournoy has been consistently making the most of his limited targets.

Flournoy struggled in an expanded role with Pickens out in Week 9, but he returned to prominence in Week 10 as the Cowboys tried to mount a furious comeback against the San Francisco 49ers. Flournoy generated seven targets in the eventual 46-40 defeat, reeling in six of them for 71 yards and a score.

With Flournoy putting up a season-best 16.1 points, breaching the nine-point line for the fifth time in the last six games and scoring his third TD in that same span, he's shown himself to be a quality WR3 for both the Cowboys and fantasy managers. His ceiling may be limited due to the superstars he plays alongside, but Flournoy is more than adequate to round out a starting fantasy lineup with.

Xavier Hutchinson, Houston Texans (2 Percent Rostered)

Xavier Hutchinson is a potential star on the rise for the Texans. He's been on fire over the last three weeks, scoring in all three games while tallying 11.9 or more points in each of those contests.

While Hutchinson got off to a slow start this year, he's been a fixture on the field and clearly earned the trust of Houston's coaching staff. That dedication began to pay off in Week 7 and has resulted in a hot streak that may not end anytime soon.

With Hutchinson tallying a season-high 15.8 points and outperforming each of his pass-catching teammates not named Nico Collins this past weekend, he's a fine waiver target for any manager seeking some receiver help. The Texans will look to get back on track by securing an easy win over the reeling Indianapolis Colts in Week 11. Hutchinson is expected to play a big role in their plans.

Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders (26 Percent Rostered)

Antonio Williams is finally starting to capitalize on the opportunity he received in the wake of Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury. The rookie caught two passes for 42 yards and a touchdown against the New York Giants on Thursday Night Football , including an impressive 31-yard scoring reception to help Washington clinch a 24-21 win.

Although his two targets weren't promising and his 12.2-point outing was largely buoyed by the TD, Williams will almost certainly have better days in the weeks ahead. He was on the field more than any other Commanders wideout on Thursday evening and averaged 6.5 targets in the two games following Washington's Week 7 bye.

While Williams needs to find a way to command targets more consistently, his unique combination of playing time, talent and a soft schedule (Washington plays the Cincinnati Bengals this weekend) makes him one of Week 11's top waiver-wire options.

Adonai Mitchell, New York Jets (33 Percent Rostered)

Adonai Mitchell looks to be in line for a larger role in the Gang Green passing attack after Omar Cooper Jr. suffered another ankle injury during the team's Week 10 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

With Cooper's breakout rookie campaign continually hindered by injury (the same ankle landed him on IR earlier this year), Mitchell will be the next man up behind entrenched star Garrett Wilson. While he caught only three of eight targets for 59 yards after Cooper exited the contest, a consistent increase in playing time and targets should give the wideout plenty of flex appeal going forward.

While Mitchell can be streaky, he has some of the best big-play potential in the business. He posted a 7/142/1 line against the Raiders in Week 8 and had several strong outings shortly after he joined the team at last year's trade deadline. Consider Mitchell a speculative flex option with tremendous upside if Cooper is sidelined.

Mark Andrews, Baltimore Ravens (53 Percent Rostered)

Mark Andrews has been one of the more disappointing fantasy tight ends this season, but Jacoby Brissett is taking over under center, which could help right the ship.

Brissett has a history of leveraging his tight ends. The journeyman most recently forged a prolific partnership with Arizona Cardinals standout Trey McBride. Developing that same sort of rapport with Andrews could help the veteran tight end return to the Pro Bowl form he displayed earlier in his career.

While managers can't bank on Andrews morphing into a true TE1 for the rest of the season, he's worth scooping up in any format he's available in, with a ceiling that rose significantly after Baltimore's trade deadline moves.

Chig Okonkwo, Washington Commanders (22 Percent Rostered)

Chig Okonkwo hasn't been the stud Washington was hoping for when they brought him in to replace Zach Ertz, but he's doing well enough to deserve starting consideration in most fantasy leagues.

The fifth-year tight end has recorded 27 receptions for 263 yards on 39 targets this season, with a recent spike in target volume suggesting his best could still be yet to come. Okonkwo has drawn at least seven targets in three of his last four games, including eight against the New York Giants during a Week 10 victory.

While Okonkwo only converted those looks into four catches for 27 yards and finished as the TE17, he'll look to improve his efficiency against a soft Cincinnati Bengals defense in Week 11.

Michael Mayer, Las Vegas Raiders (11 Percent Rostered)

Mayer had some value in deeper leagues earlier this season when the Raiders' offense was surprisingly sustaining two fantasy-relevant tight ends for stretches, but he eventually faded and hasn't posted a finish better than TE13 since Week 6. He could return to the TE1 radar if Brock Bowers ends up sitting out for a spell.

Bowers left Sunday's loss to the Seattle Seahawks with an ankle injury suffered in the first quarter. While he attempted to return shortly after the injury, he went out for the rest of the game before the half finished. It's not believed to be a significant ailment , although it could still limit or even sideline the star in Week 11.

Monitor injury news before inserting Mayer into the lineup, but the veteran projects to get plenty of volume as Fernando Mendoza's preferred safety net and red-area option if Bowers is out.

articles.title: Making the Case for the Top 2026 NFL MVP Favorites And Dark Horses Entering Week 11
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL MVP race is heating up, and it saw some interesting developments in Week 10.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL MVP race is heating up, and it saw some interesting developments in Week 10.

The star of the weekend was Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, who threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns on Sunday night and was the new MVP favorite by Monday morning. However, he was far from the only standout of Week 10.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen ran for a pair of touchdowns, while Kansas City Chiefs signal-caller Patrick Mahomes had his first five-touchdown game since 2022—and those are just some of the favorites. Players with longer MVP odds, such as running back Jahmyr Gibbs and receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, shined just as brightly.

Here, we'll make the case for the favorites and dark horses we believe have the best chances to win this year's MVP award. We'll dive into their 2026 resumes, the latest odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , and the remaining schedule and player-specific factors that could ultimately get them the nod.

Favorite: Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Bengals

Right now, it feels like the 2026 MVP is Burrow's award to lose. His performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night was incredible, but it was also pretty much par for the course for his campaign.

Burrow seems to have flipped a switch after Cincinnati's 2-2 start to the season, as if he wasn't going to allow the Bengals to waste another promising roster. He's delivered five straight wins since then and has played at an elite level.

This season, Burrow has completed 74.7 percent of his passes for 2,795 yards and 27 touchdowns, with six interceptions and a league-best 117.7 passer rating. During Sunday's win, he tied Peyton Manning's record of five straight games with four or more touchdowns.

Should Burrow extend that streak against the Washington Commanders on Monday night, it could be nearly enough to cement him as league MVP. Awards voters tend to favor a good story, and record-setting seasons usually provide them.

Plus, some voters undoubtedly believe that Burrow is due for his first career MVP.

Burrow would also finish a strong resume by carrying Cincinnati to a No. 1 seed and by beating Mahomes and the Chiefs in Week 14 along the way. He would need some help to push the Bengals into the AFC's top spot, but he certainly appears capable of getting Cincinnati through its final eight games with an undefeated record.

The only real argument against Burrow at this point is the fact that he has elite receivers in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. However, we saw Manning win five regular-season MVP awards while benefiting from strong offensive supporting casts.

Dark Horse: Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

In a different era, Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs wouldn't even be considered a mild sleeper to win the NFL MVP award. The Alabama product has been simply incredible since entering the league in 2023, and he's already rewriting the record books.

On Sunday, Gibbs surpassed Terrell Davis with the most offensive touchdowns scored (62) through a player's first four seasons. That's particularly noteworthy because Gibbs has nearly half the season left to play.

Gibbs has also become the third player under the age of 25 to rush for 50 career touchdowns. He won't turn 25 until March.

Of course, career accomplishments aren't supposed to be factored into the MVP conversation. Fortunately, Gibbs' 2026 resume is quite impressive, too. He racked up a ridiculous 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns during Detroit's Week 10 win over the New England Patriots, putting him at 1,000 rushing yards, 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 touchdowns on the season—all league highs.

There's a very real chance that Gibbs will finish the season as the league leader in rushing yards, scrimmage yards and touchdowns—and he could potentially set records.

Chris Johnson set the NFL's scrimmage-yards record at 2,509 in 2009. With eight games left on the schedule, Gibbs would need to average just under 141 scrimmage yards per game to break it. He's currently averaging 153.8 yards per game.

We haven't had a non-quarterback win the MVP award since Adrian Peterson did it in 2012. Gibbs must be considered a dark horse solely because of that fact, though he does rank among the top six favorites.

The Lions have an average-at-best defense and just lost star pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a torn ACL. If Gibbs can carry them to an NFC North title while setting a new high-water mark for all-purpose running backs, he could be the first non-QB since Peterson to be named MVP.

Allen is the current No. 2 favorite behind Burrow, and for good reason. While his passing numbers haven't been quite as impressive as those of his Bengals counterpart, the Bills QB has been sensational as a dual-threat signal-caller.

The 30-year-old has thrown for 2,223 yards, 13 touchdowns, seven interceptions, and a 97.8 QB rating. He has also rushed for 290 yards and 11 touchdowns.

Allen and Gibbs are tied for the league lead in rushing scores. On Sunday, Allen also tied Jalen Hurts for an NFL-record four straight seasons with 10 or more rushing touchdowns by a quarterback.

To overtake Burrow as league MVP, Allen may have to rely on his legs to set more records. He probably isn't going to catch up to the league leaders in passing touchdowns, but if he keeps adding to his rushing touchdown total, he'll have an MVP chance.

The current single-season record for rushing touchdowns by a quarterback is 15, held by both Allen and Hurts. Allen only needs five more rushing touchdowns to break that record, and if he can maintain his current pace, he could create a whole new benchmark by forging the 20-20 club.

Allen is on pace to deliver 25 passing touchdowns and 21 rushing touchdowns in 2026.

While Allen isn't a fresh story—having been named MVP in 2024—he could garner some extra votes because of his supporting cast. While the Bengals have a solid overall roster and two elite receivers, Allen has worked with a middling receiving corps and a defense that is a flat-out liability.

If Allen can maintain his statistical pace while keeping Buffalo in line for the AFC's No. 1 seed, he could become a two-time MVP.

Dark Horse: Kirk Cousins, QB, Minnesota Vikings

Kirk Cousins is a dark horse among quarterbacks because, statistically, he deserves to be.

In nine games with the Las Vegas Raiders and one with the Minnesota Vikings, he has been far from terrible. However, he doesn't offer much as a rushing threat, and his passing numbers have been more good than great.

Cousins has thrown for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns, eight interceptions, and a 97.1 passer rating.

However, the 38-year-old could make a legitimate case for league MVP over the final eight weeks of the season. That's because he has a chance to do something truly unprecedented.

If Cousins starts for Minnesota in the playoffs, he'll become the first quarterback in league history to start for a team in the postseason after starting games for a different team in the regular season, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

And Cousins could be the catalyst that rockets the Vikings into the playoffs.

Minnesota has boasted a championship-caliber defense all season, but subpar quarterback play had hamstrung the team's potential. The offense averaged just over 18 points per game before Cousins arrived in last week's trade. It scored 30 points in its first game with Cousins behind center.

"Man, he was dealing," center Brian O'Neill said of Cousins, per Rob Kleifield of the team's official website.

The last time Cousins played for Kevin O'Connell and the Vikings, he did so at a Pro Bowl level. If he returns to that level while making Minnesota a legitimate Super Bowl threat, he'll deserve MVP consideration.

Cousins joined the Vikings when their season appeared to be on the brink of collapse, and, right now, he feels like the most valuable player in their locker room.

Favorite: Brock Purdy, QB, San Francisco 49ers

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is the No. 3 favorite behind Burrow and Allen. He's probably the quarterback with the best chance of catching the Bengals star in passing numbers.

Purdy has completed 70.1 percent of his passes for 2,369 yards, 20 touchdowns, five interceptions, and a 115.2 passer rating. He has also rushed for 222 yards and two scores and has been far better at buying time in the pocket and creating big plays than many fans may realize.

Now, a certain portion of the NFL fanbase will always be inclined to consider Purdy a product of Kyle Shanahan and his quarterback-friendly system—despite the fact that Shanahan couldn't make that system work this beautifully with Jimmy Garoppolo or Trey Lance. Purdy also has a couple of top-tier players in Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle.

However, the rest of San Francisco's receiving corps is largely comprised of role players or stars who are past their prime, like Mike Evans and Keenan Allen, many of whom have been in and out of the lineup. Yet, Purdy has been one of the most efficient quarterbacks in the league, despite the rotating supporting cast.

The reality is that Purdy is just that good now and is playing a massive role in keeping the 49ers at the front of the NFC pack, despite numerous injuries. That strengthens his MVP candidacy.

"It's a narrative-driven award and they look like the best team in the NFC, he's playing efficiently and they haven't been healthy so he is helping lift them up," one unnamed NFL executive said, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Purdy will have to keep playing at a high level and keep San Francisco at the top of the NFL hierarchy, which will be easier said than done. However, the team's list of 2026 injuries—which has included Evans, Nick Bosa, Ricky Pearsall, Jake Tonges, Nick Martin, and others—and a tough remaining schedule could sway voters.

Over the final eight weeks, Purdy will be tested against Cousins' Vikings, Mahomes' Chiefs, the defending-champion Seattle Seahawks, and the Los Angeles Rams. If he passes those tests, he could lay claim to being the league's most valuable.

Dark Horse: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

Did you know that a wide receiver has never been named NFL MVP? A kicker has (Mark Moseley, 1982), but not a wide receiver.

That fact may be why Seattle Seahawks wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba is a true dark horse with the same odds as Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Realistically, there probably isn't a more important player in the league right now.

There might not be a more dominant player in 2026, either. Smith-Njigba has accounted for just under 52 percent of Seattle's receiving yards, and he has kept the offense humming through injuries at running back and quarterback.

On Sunday, Smith-Njigba gashed the Las Vegas Raiders' defense for 171 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions while playing with backup quarterback Drew Lock. He also became the first player since 1960 (Raymond Berry) to reach 1,200 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns through the first 10 games of a season.

The 24-year-old is currently on pace for 134 receptions and 2,052 receiving yards. That means that he has a very real shot at breaking Calvin Johnson's single-season receiving record (1,964) and becoming the league's first 2,000-yard receiver.

What's truly remarkable about Smith-Njigba's season is the fact that he's having it despite every single opposing defender knowing that the ball is coming his way. He's also been catching passes from Lock and Sam Darnold and not from an MVP-caliber quarterback like Burrow or Allen.

There hasn't been another player more valuable to his team through the first 10 weeks than Smith-Njigba.

Smith-Njigba faces long odds to become the first receiver to be named MVP largely because quarterbacks like Burrow and Allen are also having remarkable seasons. If any of the top quarterbacks stumble down the stretch, though, his window could be open.

If Smith-Njigba can carry the 6-4 Seahawks back into the postseason with a revolving door at quarterback and while setting a new single-season record, he could slip through that window like he slips through opposing secondaries.

Favorite: Patrick Mahomes, QB, Kansas City Chiefs

Mahomes has longer odds than Trevor Lawrence (+500), but may actually have a better chance of winning the MVP award than the Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback.

Lawrence has produced good numbers (2,284 yards, 21 TDs, 5 INTs, 112.8 QB rating). However, a lot of his success will be credited to second-year head coach Liam Coen and a roster that is arguably the most complete in the NFL—especially after last week's trades for Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux.

At this point in the season, Coen feels like a better bet for Coach of the Year than Lawrence is for MVP.

That said, Mahomes is still the least likely of our favorites to actually win MVP. He's done so twice, and his story isn't an exciting new one.

Only, it kind of is. Over the past year, Mahomes has seemingly faced real adversity for the first time in his career. Last year's Kansas City team wasn't playoff-caliber, and Mahomes suffered a season-ending ACL tear. He made his way back onto the field in time for Week 1, and he's played a huge role in getting the Chiefs back in the Super Bowl conversation.

Mahomes has thrown for 2,385 yards, 19 touchdowns, four interceptions, and a 106.7 QB rating. He has also rushed for 100 yards and a score.

Hurting Mahomes' chances is the fact that free-agent Kenneth Walker III largely served as the centerpiece of Kansas City's offense over the first half of the season. He missed Week 10, though, and Mahomes showed that he's still quite capable of taking over a game.

And the Chiefs' receiving corps, while bolstered by the trade for Josh Downs, is still an overall average unit.

Mahomes will need several more games like Sunday's to have a shot at MVP. He has a legitimate shot, though, because he'll get to go head-to-head with Allen, Burrow, Purdy, and reigning MVP Matthew Stafford over the final eight weeks.

If he can win all of those matchups in convincing fashion while ratcheting up the statistical production, his remarkable return from injury could push him toward MVP No. 3.

articles.title: Ideal 2027 NFL Offseason Landing Spots for QB Reclamation Projects
articles.summary: As many as 10 NFL franchises will enter the upcoming offseason with uncertainty at quarterback. The NFL draft isn't going to address everything, especially with its vaunted class not quite living up to expectations this fall. An alternative pathway exists for organizations.
articles.body:
As many as 10 NFL franchises will enter the upcoming offseason with uncertainty at quarterback. The NFL draft isn't going to address everything, especially with its vaunted class not quite living up to expectations this fall. An alternative pathway exists for organizations.

The success of Sam Darnold and Baker Mayfield in recent years forced everyone to re-examine the typical approach to a position. Situation matters so much in a quarterback's development that sometimes another first-round addition isn't the solution. That setup may ultimately lead to bigger problems. Instead, those same franchises can look at veterans with remaining upside to once again warrant consideration as an NFL starter.

As of now, it's a fair assumption that C.J. Stroud will either re-sign with or receive the franchise tag from the Houston Texans. At this point, the idea of the Philadelphia Eagles moving on from Jalen Hurts is premature. We're down to eight possibilities.

The Cleveland Browns and New York Jets own enough draft capital to ensure they land a top quarterback prospect if they choose to do so. The Miami Dolphins currently claim a top-three draft pick—which means they'll either draft a quarterback or move forward with Malik Willis at the helm for another season.

Five teams remain from those original QB-starved options. The Arizona Cardinals, Atlanta Falcons, Indianapolis Colts, Minnesota Vikings and Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves in very different organizational phases.

Each of them could benefit greatly by acquiring a formerly touted quarterback, who should be able to step in and improve the team's current setup.

The Arizona Cardinals could easily be one of the franchises that drafts a quarterback in next year's first round depending on which prospects remain available.

However, Arizona currently owns the seventh overall draft pick. The Cardinals won't be guaranteed anything at that juncture. Instead, they could turn to Mike LaFleur's roots in the NFC West before becoming the team's head coach.

Mac Jones played his best ball last season with the San Francisco 49ers. His skill set is tailor-made for the Kyle Shanahan offensive scheme. Jones was forced to start multiple games in 2025 due to Brock Purdy suffering shoulder and toe injuries.

Jones started eight games. He finished the campaign with a 69.6 completion percentage, 2,151 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. He helped keep the Niners afloat despite the team's injury woes.

LaFleur worked with both Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay before landing in the desert. His time with Shanahan would provide him with an excellent idea of how to build an offense around Jones' skill set.

Plus, he got to see Jones first-hand last season when the quarterback threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns during a Week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. LaFleur was serving as McVay's offensive coordinator at the time.

Jones' play last season reminded everyone of the rookie standout the New England Patriots originally drafted in the first round of the 2021 class. Plus, the Niners' QB2 is only 28 years old. He's ready for another opportunity, which he could find in the desert.

The Atlanta Falcons appear to be heading toward the same spot where they found themselves last offseason.

Michael Penix Jr. has yet to prove he's the long-term answer at quarterback. Thus, a short-term lottery ticket to compete with him may be the franchise's best option.

Much like the Arizona Cardinals, the Falcons aren't bad enough right now to ensure the team can draft a quarterback in next year's first round. Instead, general manager Ian Cunningham jumps back into the free-agency market to find a veteran with remaining upside.

Kyler Murray is more naturally gifted than Tua Tagovailoa. Granted, his time with Minnesota (after being released by the Arizona Cardinals) turned into a major disappointment.

In this instance, Murray may fit into Kevin Stefanski's offense a little better due to the scheme's reliance on quarterback movement and defined reads.

Murray doesn't feel like the most inspired choice based on where his career currently stands. Even so, he has previously shown flashes of brilliance. His high-end athleticism would add a completely different dynamic as part of an offense with significant surrounding talent to make everyone difficult to defend. Plus, the 2019 No. 1 overall pick doesn't turn 30 until a month before the 2027 campaign begins.

Both Sam Darnold and Baker Mayfield had stops with the Carolina Panthers and an NFC West franchise before their later-career resurgences. A similar career path may be in store for Murray after being humbled along the way.

So much uncertainty currently exists within the Indianapolis Colts organization that it's impossible to fully understand what the team will want at the quarterback position.

However, Daniel Jones shouldn't be viewed as the solution for whoever comes in to lead the team.

The Colts fired their general manager midseason. As the campaign spirals out of control, Shane Steichen probably won't remain head coach beyond Week 18. Another regime will come in and bring their preferences and philosophies.

Without knowing exactly who those people will be, the first step is understanding the Colts can release Jones with a June 1 designation and save $38 million next year. His play hasn't provided any reason why this shouldn't happen.

Anthony Richardson, whom the Colts selected fourth overall in 2023, has yet to meet expectations and is set to become a free agent. Indianapolis also lacks a first-round pick in 2027 after trading it in last year's deal for Sauce Gardner.

Indianapolis may draft a quarterback during the event's second day to groom as a future starter. But the team will need a viable option in the meantime.

Davis Mills' pending free agency provides an opportunity to swipe a player from a division rival, while adding a 28-year-old option who played well during the last time he led an NFL offense.

Mills was forced into the Houston Texans lineup as a rookie and started 26 games during his first two seasons. The 2021 third-round draft pick endured a false opportunity since the franchise was in full-blown rebuild mode.

The organization then drafted C.J. Stroud in 2023. He's now on the cusp of signing a long-term contract extension. However, Mills started three games in 2025 after Stroud suffered a concussion and looked far more comfortable leading Houston's offense.

Mills threw for 719 yards, with a five-to-one touchdown-to-interception ratio, during that stretch. The Texans won all three contests.

The Colts should be an appealing landing spot, offering a clear path to a starting job, Alec Pierce at wide receiver, Tyler Warren at tight end, a young and talented offensive line, and potentially Jonathan Taylor and/or Seth McGowan in the backfield.

Conversely, Mills would fit in nicely, particularly with Pierce, thanks to the quarterback's live arm to drive the ball down the field.

Obviously, the Colts' eventual hires will clarify the franchise's approach. As of now, Mills is as good of an option as Indianapolis could hope to field in 2027.

Kevin O'Connell's reputation as a quarterback whisperer took a major hit this fall. With J.J. McCarthy traded to the New York Giants and Kyler Murray essentially benched, the Minnesota Vikings were forced to trade for veteran Kirk Cousins to steady the ship.

Cousins could realistically come back for another season. However, the Vikings should look for a younger option since their current starter turns 39 before the start of the 2027 campaign.

Interestingly, the Vikings have ties to a Seattle Seahawks quarterback not named Sam Darnold. Minnesota's general manager, Nolan Teasley, worked as part of the Seahawks' scouting department from 2013 to '25, serving as the franchise's assistant general manager during the final three seasons. He was part of a front office that acquired/signed Drew Lock not once, but twice.

Lock has played exceptionally well in Darnold's absence this season. In fact, Seattle has won all four games in which Lock started. The 2019 second-round draft pick was once a highly regarded prospect who finally appears to fully grasp the game now as opposed to earlier in his professional career.

Plus, his relationship with Darnold can provide insight into the Vikings coaching staff and organization.

Aaron Rodgers' inevitable retirement is the only thing known about the Pittsburgh Steelers' quarterback setup coming out of this season.

From there, the Steelers should pursue multiple avenues to ensure they're set at the game's most important position.

The organization may decide it likes what it has in Drew Allar and/or Will Howard. However, the Steelers shouldn't bank on that approach when the team's front office can still add another option.

J.J. McCarthy started to look like the quarterback prospect who once warranted the 10th overall pick in the 2024 draft. Granted, he's already with his second team after being traded by the Minnesota Vikings.

Even so, McCarthy has performed well enough in a small sample size to create intrigue regarding the New York Giants' long-term quarterback plans. If he ultimately takes the job, Jaxson Dart could then become a trade target.

For now, Dart remains the presumed long-term preference in New York. The Giants only traded a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to obtain McCarthy's services. The team's front office could easily profit by flipping the quarterback next offseason. As of now, Pittsburgh owns extra third-, sixth- and seventh-round picks, as well as five of its original selections, for next year's draft.

Pittsburgh doesn't operate in a fashion where a full-blown rebuild is expected. As such, a top quarterback prospect almost certainly won't be available through the draft. Instead, the Steelers should fill their quarterback room with talented, young individuals and allow one to emerge as QB1.

articles.title: Week 11 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Smartest Matchups to Exploit, Sleeper Plays and More
articles.summary: It's getting to be crunch time in most fantasy leagues, as the playoffs are on the horizon. Unfortunately, navigating the final stretch won't be an easy process for many managers. Injuries continue to negatively impact rosters, and we saw several more stars go down in Week 10.
articles.body:
It's getting to be crunch time in most fantasy leagues, as the playoffs are on the horizon. Unfortunately, navigating the final stretch won't be an easy process for many managers. Injuries continue to negatively impact rosters, and we saw several more stars go down in Week 10.

Drake Maye, Brock Bowers, Woody Marks, and Geno Smith were just some of the key players who exited with injuries over the weekend.

Additionally, we'll have six teams on bye in Week 11: the Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots, and Seattle Seahawks.

Many managers will have to lean on second-tier stars and sleepers this week. Let's examine some of the best and worst matchups for point-per-reception (PPR) play.

Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud had a rough overall outing against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. He and the offense stalled in the second half, which helped Cleveland record yet another comeback victory.

However, Stroud still threw three touchdown passes and finished with 21.4 fantasy points. He should be trusted on a short week against the Indianapolis Colts this week. The Colts have been far less competitive than the Browns and have surrendered an average of 19.8 fantasy points to opposing QBs.

J.J. McCarthy has been a fairly solid starter for the New York Giants since taking the reins of the offense. However, he can't be trusted this week against a surging Jacksonville Jaguars defense.

Jacksonville has surrendered an average of just 16.4 fantasy points to opposing QBs, and its defense is about to get better. Trade additions Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III are expected to debut for the Jaguars in New York.

Managers seeking a fill-in quarterback should consider Cam Ward, who is rostered in only nine percent of fantasy leagues. He has topped 20 fantasy points in each of his last two games and has a favorable matchup against a suspect Dallas Cowboys defense this week.

Titans running back Tony Pollard should be a strong play against a bad Cowboys defense in Week 11. He struggled to find running room against a good Jaguars defense on Sunday but came through for fantasy managers with his receiving.

Pollard caught eight passes, found the end zone, and finished with 23.9 fantasy points. Dallas, meanwhile, has surrendered an average of 30 fantasy points to opposing backfields this season.

Alvin Kamara came through for fantasy managers with three receptions, a rushing touchdown, and 16.4 fantasy points on Sunday. However, he was not a focal point of the New Orleans Saints' ground game with Travis Etienne Jr. back in the lineup.

With Etienne and Audric Estimé in the Saints' backfield, Kamara will have a limited floor moving forward. He is a very risky play this week against a terrific Chicago Bears defensive front coming off its bye. The Bears have surrendered an average of only 18.6 fantasy points to opposing backfields.

Sleeper: Emari Demercado, Houston Texans

Emari Demercado, who is rostered in only one percent of leagues, must be considered a deep sleeper. However, he could see a significant workload on Thursday against the Colts. David Montgomery has been out with a groin injury, and Marks exited Sunday's loss with a concussion.

The Miami Dolphins recently placed starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve and pivoted to late offseason addition Kyle McCord. While the change did impact Miami's offense, it didn't hinder wide receiver Caleb Douglas as much as one might have expected.

Douglas still reached double-digit fantasy points in Week 10, finishing with 71 yards on three catches. This week, he'll face a Buffalo Bills defense that has surrendered the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers.

After trading Kirk Cousins, the Las Vegas Raiders pivoted to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Naturally, that impacted the offense significantly. Mendoza is still building a rapport with his pass-catchers, which is an issue for wideout Tre Tucker.

Tucker had just one reception in Week 10, and he'll be hard to trust this week, even if Bowers isn't at 100 percent. The Denver Broncos have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers.

Pat Bryant is still only rostered in seven percent of fantasy leagues. That will change if he has a big game against the Raiders this week, which is entirely possible. Bryant logged 15.6 fantasy points in his last game, while Las Vegas has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing WRs.

Top Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups 🏈

The Cincinnati Bengals rolled over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night, leaning on their passing attack along the way. For the second straight week, though, tight end Mike Gesicki was largely an afterthought.

While Gesicki last produced double-digit fantasy points in Week 8, he should return to form against the Washington Commanders on Monday night. Only the Detroit Lions have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing TEs than Washington.

While McCord was able to get the ball to Miami's receivers, he clearly doesn't have the chemistry with tight end Greg Dulcich that Willis was beginning to develop. After recording at least four targets and two receptions in four straight games, Dulcich finished without a catch on two targets.

Managers shouldn't expect Dulcich to bounce back against the Bills, who have surrendered an average of only 10.9 fantasy points to opposing TEs this season.

Sleeper: Michael Mayer, Las Vegas Raiders

Bowers is expected to play in Week 11, but fellow tight end Michael Mayer could have some sleeper value. The Raiders will undoubtedly look to get Mendoza some easy reads, and Mayer should be a strong outlet option. And while Denver has been good defensively overall, it has surrendered the third-most fantasy points (tied) to opposing TEs.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for LSU OT Jordan Seaton
articles.summary: Jordan Seaton projects as a starting NFL left tackle with legitimate first-round traits as Bleacher Report's OT1. Seaton is a fluid, long-limbed tackle with high-end lateral range, grip-strength and recovery ability in pass protection. His movement skills and active hands allow him to stay square, control the high side and re-leverage after initial stress, while his length and latch-strength can engulf defenders once attached. His initial firmness can still be stressed by long-arm power when the hand-fit is compromised, and his timing and body control in the run game remain inconsistent.
articles.body:
Jordan Seaton projects as a starting NFL left tackle with legitimate first-round traits as Bleacher Report's OT1. Seaton is a fluid, long-limbed tackle with high-end lateral range, grip-strength and recovery ability in pass protection. His movement skills and active hands allow him to stay square, control the high side and re-leverage after initial stress, while his length and latch-strength can engulf defenders once attached. His initial firmness can still be stressed by long-arm power when the hand-fit is compromised, and his timing and body control in the run game remain inconsistent.

The junior prospect is a 6'5", 311-pound lineman, who arrived at LSU after spending his first two seasons with the Colorado Buffaloes. He entered college as a consensus 5-star recruit and the No. 1 offensive tackle in the 2024 class.

Seaton started 22 games at left tackle during his two seasons at Colorado, earning Freshman All-America honors in 2024 and second-team All-Big 12 honors in 2025 before transferring to LSU.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

High-end lateral quickness and range in pass protection to intersect wide alignments, stay connected through the corner and recover when initially stressed.

Uses his length and grip-strength to engulf rushers once attached, with the hand-strength to re-engage, steer and sustain through secondary moves.

Natural feel working combinations and climbing to the second level, with the acceleration and lateral range to connect on linebackers outside his initial track.

Carries active, well-timed hands in pass protection, with effective double-under fits and the ability to clench, circle and torque rushers once attached. Shows the recovery strength to re-anchor after absorbing an initial jolt.

Initial hand fit and firmness can be compromised against long-arm power, particularly when his outside hand misses or lands high, forcing him to recover after conceding leverage.

Snap timing and body control can be inconsistent, leading to late departures, oversteps and compromised positioning on backside cutoffs.

Needs to sustain his leverage more consistently in the run game rather than allowing defenders to stack, shed or backdoor him after initially reaching advantageous positioning.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Athletic starting LT with high-end range, active hands, grip and recovery traits.

He creates real displacement in the run game, handles movement with patience and has enough short-area quickness to execute in Iowa's zone scheme. However, his high-side range will be questionable against NFL speed, which could eventually push him inside to guard despite a strong overall tackle skill set.

Trevor Lauck is a powerful, controlled tackle with very good play-strength, strong hands and a stout anchor. He creates real displacement in the run game, handles movement with patience and has enough short-area quickness to execute in Iowa's zone scheme. However, his high-side range will be questionable against NFL speed, which could eventually push him inside to guard despite a strong overall tackle skill set.

Lauck is a 6'5", 314-pound offensive line prospect who arrived at Iowa as a 4-star recruit in the 2023 class.. He played in three games in 2024 before taking over at left tackle in 2025, starting all 13 games and earning third-team All-Big Ten honors while helping Iowa win the Joe Moore Award. He remained the starting left tackle in 2026.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Excellent play-strength and core-strength allow him to absorb force, stay connected and create substantial displacement once he enters the drive phase.

Strong hands with good grip, refit ability and circle/clamp technique to regain control after initial contact and engulf rushers once attached.

Stout against power in pass protection, consistently dropping his hips, rooting his feet and conceding minimal pocket depth against bull rushes.

Good short-area quickness and processing in the run game, with the ability to execute backside cutoffs, adjust to movement and locate work when uncovered.

High-side range is the primary concern as an offensive tackle projection, with true edge speed capable of turning the corner when he has to defend significant space.

Can get caught leaning when defenders capture his outside shoulder and work back across his face, stressing his recovery athleticism.

Occasionally plays too high and exposes the inside shoulder, allowing rushers to pry him open despite his strength advantage.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Notre Dame IOL Anthonie Knapp
articles.summary: Anthonie Knapp is a powerful, controlled guard with heavy hands, a sturdy anchor and outstanding play-strength once attached. He combines that force with good lateral quickness, giving him range on zone tracks, combinations and second-level work. Quick cross-face movement can expose occasional oversets and late inside recovery, but he projects as a starting NFL guard with legitimate first-round traits.
articles.body:
Anthonie Knapp is a powerful, controlled guard with heavy hands, a sturdy anchor and outstanding play-strength once attached. He combines that force with good lateral quickness, giving him range on zone tracks, combinations and second-level work. Quick cross-face movement can expose occasional oversets and late inside recovery, but he projects as a starting NFL guard with legitimate first-round traits.

Knapp is a 6'5", 304-pound offensive line prospect who arrived at Notre Dame as a 3-star recruit in the 2024 class. He immediately became Notre Dame's starting left tackle as a true freshman, making 15 starts in 2024 before starting 12 more games at left tackle in 2025. He moved inside to left guard for the 2026 season.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

High-end play-strength with heavy hands and a strong lower half to absorb force, generate lift and create displacement after the initial fit.

Patient and powerful in pass protection, using tight double-under fits, strong hand placement and a sturdy anchor to shut down power near the line of scrimmage.

Better mover than his power-first profile suggests, with good lateral footwork on zone tracks, clean backside cutoffs and enough range to climb and connect on linebackers.

Excellent sustain and finishing ability once attached, consistently running his feet, torquing defenders and preventing clean sheds back into the play.

Can settle slightly too far outside in pass protection, allowing quick cross-face moves to trap his inside hand and stress his recovery.

Sudden redirects against fast-flowing second-level targets can cause him to step underneath himself and be tardy to redirect.

Has isolated balance and body-control lapses on pulls or through traffic, while his target alignment in space can be inconsistent.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Powerful, heavy-handed guard with high-end play strength, anchor and functional movement skills
