articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Kentucky OT Lance Heard
articles.summary: Lance Heard is a big, high-cut tackle with legitimate length, heavy hands and the grip strength to control rushers once he establishes first meaningful contact. His hand usage has developed into a real strength, particularly his snatch/trap timing and ability to play long, but his range is more adequate than high-end and inconsistent leverage/body control can still lead to compression or late sheds. He projects as a starting-caliber tackle whose length and hands give him margin for error, but he needs greater consistency marrying his feet, hips and hands through the entire rep.
articles.body:
Lance Heard is a big, high-cut tackle with legitimate length, heavy hands and the grip strength to control rushers once he establishes first meaningful contact. His hand usage has developed into a real strength, particularly his snatch/trap timing and ability to play long, but his range is more adequate than high-end and inconsistent leverage/body control can still lead to compression or late sheds. He projects as a starting-caliber tackle whose length and hands give him margin for error, but he needs greater consistency marrying his feet, hips and hands through the entire rep.

Heard is a 6'6", 325-pound offensive line prospect who arrived at LSU as a 5-star recruit in the 2023 class. He appeared in all 12 regular-season games as a true freshman and made one start at right tackle before transferring to Tennessee. Heard started 11 games at left tackle in 2024, missing two games due to injury, then started all 12 games there in 2025 before transferring to Kentucky for the 2026 season.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Excellent length and heavy hands give him the ability to establish first meaningful contact, play at extension and control rushers from outside his frame before they can fully access his chest.

Advanced flashes of hand usage, particularly against long-arm rushes. His snatch/trap timing consistently showed up against LSU, allowing him to clear the rusher's post hand, disrupt balance and regain control without conceding significant ground.

Legitimate stopping power when his pad level, hips and hands arrive together. He can sit down on direct power, create separation and stone rushers when he gets underneath them rather than allowing his high-cut frame to dictate the rep.

Physical run blocker with strong grip and enough movement ability to execute kickouts, down blocks and second-level assignments. His upper-body strength allows him to wall off defenders and generate displacement even when the lower-body positioning is not perfect.

High-cut build makes leverage and anchor consistency an ongoing issue. When his hips stay high or his upper body gets ahead of his feet, power can compress him and defenders can work underneath his frame.

Edge range is adequate rather than a defining strength. His length allows him to survive rushers reaching the corner, but NFL-caliber speed can put him into trail position and force him to rely on late hand strength and recovery.

Sustain and body control remain inconsistent. He can win first contact and still lose the rep late when his feet stop, his base narrows or he leans into the block, leading to clean sheds across his face.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Long, heavy-handed tackle with advanced snatch/trap ability, functional power and adequate edge range to become a starter.

Workout numbers and data will be added at a later date.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Ohio State IOL Austin Siereveld
articles.summary: Austin Siereveld is a powerful, steady blocker with strong hands, a sturdy anchor and good processing skills. He consistently gets himself into favorable positions where his play-strength can take over, but his range against true edge speed limits his projection at tackle. He's better served at guard, where his anchor, first-level control and awareness give him developmental starting upside.

Austin Siereveld is a powerful, steady blocker with strong hands, a sturdy anchor and good processing skills. Sturdy anchor and good play-strength allow him to absorb direct power, clamp rushers and keep the pocket firm once his base is established.

Strong, controlled hands with the ability to refit, snatch and torque defenders when they lean or lose their center of gravity.

Processes movement quickly and efficiently, showing awareness to pass off threats, close interior space and find work when uncovered.

Effective run-blocker with good first-level control, combo timing and enough power to create lateral or vertical displacement before working off the block.

Range against true edge speed is adequate at best, with wide alignments and high-side speed forcing him into trail positions around the top of the pocket.

Can be a tick late transitioning into his anchor, allowing power to generate initial compression before he settles.

Limited recovery margin in space makes guard a cleaner projection than tackle against NFL-caliber speed and counter ability.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Powerful, steady guard with strong hands, processing ability and added tackle experience

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for SMU OT PJ Williams
articles.summary: P.J. Williams is a big, long tackle prospect with heavy hands, functional range and the strength to control rushers once attached. He projects as a developmental offensive tackle, with starting traits whose consistency will depend on improving his footwork, body control and hand placement.

He projects as a developmental offensive tackle, with starting traits whose consistency will depend on improving his footwork, body control and hand placement.

Williams is a 6'5", 306-pound offensive line prospect, who arrived to Texas A&M as a 4-star recruit in the 2022 class. He transferred to SMU following his freshman season at Texas A&M.

Williams appeared in 12 games with four starts at left tackle in 2023 before starting all 14 games in 2024, including 11 at right tackle. He started all 13 games in 2025 and earned second-team All-ACC honors.

Brandon is the author of the Trench Warfare newsletter , which focuses exclusively on offensive and defensive line evaluation. He also contributes as an analyst to Establish the Run , serves as the scouting coordinator for OL Masterminds and is a selection committee member for the Joe Moore Award .

Big, long frame with strong hands to clench rushers once attached, circle high-side moves and widen the edge beyond the quarterback.

Sturdy against power when his feet and hands are synchronized, with the upper-body strength and grip to absorb bull-rushes, refit and halt momentum.

Generates good displacement when he can square up first-level targets, using his size, leg drive and hand-strength to wash defenders out of the lane.

Physical finisher in space who can overwhelm smaller second- and third-level targets once he gets them lined up, with several examples seen on film of driving and burying defenders.

High-cut build and lower-body stiffness create lag when redirecting, leading to oversets, wide bases and lunging against sudden inside counters or across-face movement.

Too often exposes his chest or relies on wrapping and body contact rather than consistently establishing clean hand leverage, making it easier for defenders to stack, lift or shed him.

Timing and body control are inconsistent climbing to the second level, while his anchor can arrive late when power catches him with a compromised base.

PLAYER ARCHETYPE : Long, heavy-handed tackle with starting traits whose lower-body stiffness creates pass-protection volatility

Excellent snap timing with light, urgent feet to close space quickly and consistently establish first meaningful contact before rushers can get into his frame.

Active, powerful hands with an effective inside hand, double-under fits and the grip-strength to clamp, torque and redirect rushers once attached.

Shows real explosiveness through contact in the run game, with the acceleration and leg drive to create displacement through angle blocks, down blocks and drive phases.

Athletic pass protector with the range to stay square against high-side movement, recover his anchor against power and smoothly redirect when his initial positioning is sound.

Can become passive or late with his hands, allowing rushers to clear Okunlola's frame before he establishes control.

Inside recovery can become choppy when he gets vertical too quickly, leaving a soft inside shoulder and compromising his body position against counters.

Processing and body control remain somewhat inconsistent, with isolated examples of leaving the first level too early on combos, arriving late with help and lunging when movement changes suddenly.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Miami QB Darian Mensah
articles.summary: Darian Mensah is an innately accurate pocket passer with great ball placement, making him a wide receiver's best friend. He's a natural thrower with clean, compact mechanics.
articles.body:
Darian Mensah is an innately accurate pocket passer with great ball placement, making him a wide receiver's best friend. He's a natural thrower with clean, compact mechanics.

Mensah played for three different programs in three years after beginning his career with the Tulane Green Wave then transferring to Duke last season. He led the Blue Devils to an ACC title and emerged as the championship game's MVP before transferring again, this time to the Miami Hurricanes.

The underclassman is a former 3-star recruit from the 2023 class.

Dame is the lead host of the Locked On NFL Draft podcast. Previously, he spent three years as a senior draft analyst for The Draft Network while evaluating draft prospects as the founder of The Scouting Room .

Excellent pre-snap recognition. Mensah identifies coverage shells and makes proper checks at the line of scrimmage.

Good post-snap diagnosis. He recognizes disguises, rotations and blitzes without hesitation.

Great anticipatory passer based on the coverage and leverage. He throws receivers open, too.

High-level accuracy and ball placement. His throws lead receivers away from defenders.

Displays good decision-making and operates as a risk-averse passer who avoids turnover-worthy plays, taking check-downs when available and necessary.

Plays with a good internal clock to sense pressure and get the ball out, while not displaying with "happy feet" when working from the pocket.

Functional mobility inside the pocket, steps up and slides to avoid pressure. He can also tuck the ball and scramble for positive gains, if necessary. He displays enough straight-line speed to move the chains.

Arm strength and velocity are above average, but Mensah lacks elite all-around arm talent.

Lacks off-platform power/strength to make throws down the field without a clean base.

Must cut down the tendency to throw off his back foot when facing a free runner from the defense.

Path to success will be more mental than physical at the next level.

Player Archetype : Mensah is a smooth and poised operator from the pocket. He is highly accurate and quick processing similar to a CJ Stroud or Joe Burrow, his mental processing and natural throwing ability make him a safe NFL projection with a high floor.

Innate playmaking ability; keeps plays alive with his legs and

Layers throws well to get up and down into the void versus zone defense

articles.title: Zay Flowers' Costly Fumble Addressed by HC Minter in Viral Video After Ravens' Loss to Chargers
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens coach Jesse Minter offered a veiled critique of Zay Flowers after the star wide receiver coughed up the ball late in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens coach Jesse Minter offered a veiled critique of Zay Flowers after the star wide receiver coughed up the ball late in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers.

Minter told reporters following the game Flowers should always maintain a level of situational awareness.

"Know when the journey is over and know when you're fighting for extra yards," he said.

With a little over two minutes left in the game, Flowers hauled in a 15-yard pass. Rather than going down after Chargers cornerback Tarheeb Still came in to make the tackle, he tried to gain an extra yard or two, only for Still to rip the ball out.

The Ravens eventually retook possession but had just 11 seconds on the clock while starting on their own 20-yard line. Jacoby Brissett's Hail Mary attempt from inside his own territory fell incomplete as time expired.

Amplifying the frustration of fans, this has been a pattern for Flowers well before Monday night.

Turning shorter and medium-range throws into big plays is part of what makes the two-time Pro Bowler effective. To Minter's point, however, there are moments when a wideout simply has to take what the defense gives him and move on to the next play.

Without Flowers' fumble, the Ravens were set up well to at least get close enough for a game-tying field goal. Instead, the turnover doomed Baltimore to a fifth straight defeat.

articles.title: Cowboys break embarrassing 4-year record on a single Week 10 play
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are breaking records in all the worst ways and in Week 10 they found a new way to break a four-year record.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are historically poor on defense. Such a statement was true last season and it remains true this season. After giving up 584 yards and 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10, they rank last in the NFL in EPA allowed per drive for the second year in a row.

Former head coach and current ESPN analyst Rex Ryan said Dallas was "the worst coached defense I think I've ever seen," and it's hard to argue otherwise. The Cowboys have somehow lost three games this season in which they scored 30+ points, tying an NFL record through the first 10 weeks of a season. And now it seems the Cowboys are also breaking records on a play-by-play basis.

Seth Walder, ESPN's Next Gen Stats analyst, revealed that Deebo Samuel's 70-yard touchdown run in the third quarter produced the most expected rush yards in roughly four years. The end-around caught Dallas so out of position, at the time Samuel began rounding the corner, 10 of Dallas' 11 defenders were still outside of the wrong hashmark.

With a six-to-one blocking advantage, the 49ers easily ran to paydirt on the play, producing a whopping 5.7 in EPA and pushing San Francisco's lead up to 31-19. It was an embarrassment only surpassed by Christian McCaffery's 74-yard touchdown reception a quarter earlier, but it won the day in its historic significance and in its ability to serve as a perfect illustration of Dallas' 2026 defensive woes.

It wasn't just that the Cowboys fell for the play fake, but it was that players abandoned assignments and responsibilities to play run and chase in the wrong direction. This undisciplined playing style has been a signature trait of the Cowboys over the years, firmly standing in the way of any defensive overhaul Christian Parker or any other defensive coordinator wishes to embark on.

The Cowboys are breaking records by the week. Will they continue their record setting ways or is now when they finally put the brakes on their defensive downward spiral?

articles.title: Everything Harbaugh, Herbert Said After Chargers Snap Losing Streak with Win vs. Ravens
articles.summary: After snapping their season-long losing streak with a 23-20 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night, Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh and quarterback Justin Herbert felt a sigh relief.
articles.body:
After snapping their season-long losing streak with a 23-20 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night, Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh and quarterback Justin Herbert felt a sigh relief.

Speaking to reporters following the victory, Harbaugh praised the "fight" his team has shown throughout a difficult season and hopes this will lead to more wins going forward.

Herbert acknowledged the "tough year" the Chargers have had, but then echoed his coach's sentiments that everyone was "excited" throughout the game and to get their first win.

"It hasn't gone our way this year and for those guys to continue to fight, not point fingers, and stick together — they've earned it and I'm really happy for them," Herbert said.

Harbaugh was also very complimentary toward the defense, particularly the job they did holding Derrick Henry to 10 rushing yards on 10 carries.

"Heck of a run wall, [a] big emphasis on that," Harbaugh said. "Just trying not to let [Henry] get started ... guys just battled the whole night."

On the offensive side, Herbert praised the protection up front that helped the Chargers rack up a season-high 160 yards on the ground.

"It was awesome," Herbert said. "It was so much up front, they work so hard ... and [Hampton] is about as talented as it gets, the way he runs."

Herbert got to show off his wheels with 51 rushing yards, including 22 on his touchdown run in the first quarter. Omarion Hampton finished with 105 yards on 22 carries for the second 100-yard game of his career.

Dating back to last season, the Chargers had lost 11 straight games that was tied for the longest such streak in franchise history. Their last victory was 330 days ago against the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 21, 2025.

Now, Harbaugh, Herbert and the Chargers will look to keep their positive momentum going as they prepare to host the New York Jets on Sunday at SoFi Stadium.

articles.title: Lions' Aidan Hutchinson confirmed to have torn ACL, ending his 2026 season
articles.summary: Hutchinson sustained the injury during Detroit's win over the Patriots in Munich, celebrating a sack early in the game.
articles.body:
Fears that Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his right knee were confirmed after additional exams, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . Though tests reportedly revealed no other significant damage to Hutchinson's knee, he is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season with the injury.

On Tuesday, Lions head coach Dan Campbell confirmed that injury, saying "it stinks" and that Hutchinson will come out of it better on the other side.

Hutchinson injured his knee on the Lions' first defensive series versus the New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich. After sacking New England's Drake Maye, Detroit's fifth-year star jumped in celebration and landed awkwardly on his right leg. Hutchinson immediately went to the turf. As teammates and players approached, he gestured to the front of his right knee.

Campbell added Tuesday that he will not speak with Hutchinson about celebrating plays. Campbell said he didn't want to take emotion out of the game.

Hutchinson reportedly underwent an MRI after Detroit's 35-10 win that showed a torn ACL. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the defensive end would undergo further testing when the team returned to the U.S. before making an official announcement.

"We'll know more when we get back in the States," head coach Dan Campbell said postgame, via the Detroit News' Nolan Bianchi . "Anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy."

Meanwhile, a fan captured video of Hutchinson in a wheelchair at the airport prior to the Lions traveling back to Michigan on Sunday.

Maye sustained an injury to his ankle on the same play and the Patriots fear the QB may have suffered a fracture that would end his season . The third-year star stayed in Germany for additional testing that could determine if he needs surgery, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed during a radio interview Monday.

In nine games this season, Hutchinson recorded 6 sacks and 24 total tackles in addition to 1 pass defended and 1 forced fumble.

Hutchinson's torn ACL is the second serious, season-ending injury that he has sustained during his NFL career. During the 2024 season, he suffered a broken fibula and tibia in his left leg during a Week 6 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Hutchinson recovered to play in all 17 games last year, compiling 14.5 sacks.

The Lions' 2022 first-round draft pick (No. 2 overall) out of Michigan, Hutchinson has been named to two Pro Bowls and earned second-team All-Pro honors during his career. He's compiled 49 sacks in 65 games with 200 tackles and 5 interceptions.

Last year, Hutchinson signed a four-year, $180 million contract extension (including $141 million in guaranteed money). That extension kicks in next season following the fifth-year option the Lions picked up this year.
